candidate_sources.docs/host-api.md: Controller verbs: run(value), close(), disposeChild(), snapshot(), dispose(). Injected notify(value) returns a deferred payload {value,events}; write(value) observes a state write, returned(payload) observes each operation completion. Native callback return port corresponds to the original awaited run result. Shell policy is independent from modal state; close is terminal for a modal instance.

checkpoints: Run while open and resolve while still open: the modal value is updated, env.write receives that value, the React view publishes, and env.returned receives the payload.
Run while open, call close before resolution, then resolve: no modal value update, env.write, or React publication occurs; env.returned still receives the payload.
Resolve after component disposal/unmount: no modal state update, write, or publication occurs; operation completion remains observable through env.returned.
Verify close remains terminal for that modal instance and snapshot continues to expose the existing {value,closed} shape.
Verify the application-shell subscription and its ability to receive results after a view closes are unchanged.
Perform the public JavaScript syntax/build check, recognizing that it does not test business behavior.
forbidden_effects: Do not migrate, cancel, retire, or otherwise alter the application-shell subscription.
Do not treat closing the alerts modal as closing or disposing the application shell.
Do not let a deferred notification mutate modal-owned value, call env.write, or publish a React update after the modal instance is closed or disposed.
Do not suppress the operation-completion observation env.returned merely because modal publication is no longer permitted.
Do not change the documented controller verbs or snapshot shape.
Do not edit tests, configuration, dependency locks, or files outside business code.
lifecycle_identity: The relevant publication owner is the particular alerts-modal instance represented by Workspace state.
close is terminal for that modal instance; a result resolving after that boundary is stale for modal-state publication.
dispose/unmount also closes and disposes the same modal-owned state through the existing cleanup.
The application shell has an independent, application-level lifetime and must not inherit the modal instance's terminal-close policy.

obligations.text: A deferred notify result may update s.value, call env.write, and publish a React render only if the originating alerts-modal instance is still open when the result callback executes.
Calling close must immediately establish the terminal modal boundary so any later notify completion cannot update or publish modal state.
Disposal/unmount must retain its existing close/dispose effect and prevent later notify completions from updating or publishing modal state.
Every notify operation completion must continue to be reported through env.returned(result), including when modal-state publication is suppressed after close or disposal.
The repair must be confined to the modal subscription behavior; the independent application-shell subscription and its lifecycle policy must remain unchanged.
Preserve the existing public controller verbs, notification payload handling, open-modal value/write/publication behavior, and snapshot result shape.

ordering_barriers: The modal's open/closed status must be checked in the deferred notify completion callback, after the result arrives and immediately before modal value mutation, env.write, and publication.
close or dispose occurring before deferred completion must win over that completion for modal-state publication.
env.returned(result) remains an operation-completion observation after the publication decision and must occur whether publication is allowed or suppressed.
preservation: When a notification resolves while the modal is open, preserve assignment of result.value to modal state, env.write of that value, and React publication.
Preserve passing the original deferred payload unchanged to env.returned.
Preserve close as terminal for a modal instance and dispose as setting both closed and disposed.
Preserve all documented controller verbs: run(value), close(), disposeChild(), snapshot(), and dispose().
Preserve the application shell's independent ownership and ability to receive a result after a view has closed.
scope: Business behavior in src/Workspace.jsx associated with the alerts-modal deferred notification callback.
The lifecycle boundary established by the existing close and dispose paths only as needed to guard modal publication.
No change to the independent application-shell subscription.

supporting_evidence.quote: A notification received after the alerts modal is closed still updates the modal's state. Fix the issue. Change only the modal subscription; do not migrate the application-shell subscription.

Native callback return port corresponds to the original awaited run result. Shell policy is independent from modal state; close is terminal for a modal instance.

triggers: A run(input) call begins a deferred env.notify(input) operation.
The notify promise resolves and enters its completion callback.
close() marks the modal instance closed before or after a run begins.
dispose() or React effect cleanup marks the instance closed and disposed.
A result resolves while the modal remains open.
A result resolves after the modal has closed or been disposed.
